cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Trade Operations Analyst role on the Investment Operations team in Boston. The posting centers on confirming and matching trades, resolving settlement issues, clearing nostro breaks and reconciling cash and positions daily. That is reconciliation work, and it is the part of finance I have spent the most time on.

At AMG Family Dental in Belmont, I run financial operations for a practice serving more than 1,000 patients a year. I identified and recovered more than $500K in annual revenue by improving our reporting and reconciliation process in Dentrix. I also automated our weekly insurance payment reconciliation with Python, which cut processing time from 5 hours to 1 and flagged underpaid claims for follow-up. Your posting asks analysts to automate end-to-end processes where possible, and that is exactly how I approach recurring breaks: find the pattern, script the check, and spend my time on the exceptions.

Earlier, as a Financial Analyst Intern at Northrop Grumman, I audited more than 100 financial models for accuracy, compliance and internal controls, and I presented findings to senior leadership. That gave me a control mindset I still use. I am comfortable in Excel at an advanced level, I have used SAP and Deltek Cobra to maintain data integrity, and I have a Bloomberg Terminal background from my master's program in International Economics and Finance at Brandeis.

I have not worked on an equities, bonds or swaps settlement desk, and I would be learning the product and custodian side from the team. What I bring is detail orientation, a habit of documenting how a break was resolved, and the willingness to partner with front office, technology and operations teams.

Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the chance to talk about the team.

Sincerely,
Alexander Airapetian
